About CCH iFirm Common, Jobs, Accounts Receivable and Invoice APIs
The Common API module allows you to interact with the
CCH iFirm
common areas (Contacts, Users, Contact Security and Security Profiles) externally from the application using HTTP requests. With this module, you can trigger different actions in
CCH iFirm
such as extracting data, setting data, creating Contacts or Users and more without the need to be in a browser. This way, you can enhance your firmâs workflow by developing your own home-made solutions integrated with
CCH iFirm
or simply merge your existing tools with
CCH iFirm
.
The Jobs, Accounts Receivable and Invoice APIs allow you to interact with the
CCH iFirm
Jobs & Billing module, where you can create and update jobs, add accounts receivable transactions and extract invoice information.
Looking for information on the
CCH iFirm Taxprep
Web API, consult the
Taxprep Web API
help topic.
Authentication
To use the APIs, you will need to set up OAuth 2.0 to implement authentication and authorization. It is required to have an authorization flow so your users can authorize your app to connect with
CCH iFirm
. If users grant permission, our server sends an authorization code back to your app. Your app exchanges this code for access tokens. Please consult the Knowledge Base article for more details:
How do I implement Oauth2 token authentication for CCH iFirm API?
Errors and messages (response body)
The API endpoints can return different errors in the response body depending on the context of the request. For more information about our different error messages, please refer to the Swagger API discovery tool.
HTTP Errors and Messages
With the API, you might receive an HTTP error, like a 404 Not found error. In many scenarios, different messages were included to help you troubleshoot your requests. For more information, please refer to the Swagger API discovery tool.
Rate limiting
Different types of API requests to
CCH iFirm
APIs are subject to different rate limits. The endpoints are separated in 2 categories which are Group A and Group B. You can consult the list of available endpoints to validate in which category they belong in this section of the help topic:
API Endpoints Specifications and Discovery Tool
.
The Group A of requests are limited to 30 requests per minute and 3000 requests per day. The Group B of requests are limited to 6 requests per minute and 125 requests per day. Plans that allow for more requests are available. Contact your solution consultant for more information.
A 429 error, Too many requests, is returned when the number of requests limit per minute or day is reached. Note that the rate-limit algorithm that track the number of requests for the Common API includes a margin of error that may lead to imperfect count before you get an error for exceeding a threshold.

Here is a quick guide using the
getsecurityrolesforprofile
endpoint to explain how you can experiment with the different endpoints applying the API specifications:
Expand the section corresponding to the action you would like to perform with the API.
Expand the endpoint that you are interested to try out.
Click on the example value of the body (optional), to paste the example into the
requests
fieldâthis will enable you to start with an already valid structure.
Complete the
profileID
field (e.g., 1, 2, 3 or 4).
To launch the request, click the
Try it out!
button.
Once the request has been completed, the following information is provided:
A curl example of your request.
The URL of your request, including the parameters that were set at points 4 and 5.
The response body.
The response code.
The different response headers.
